newsitem.title: UK: Go-Ahead share dealing questioned by UK MP.
newsitem.headline: Go-Ahead share dealing questioned by UK MP.

text.p: A British member of Parliament on Wednesday raised questions about possible insider dealing in shares in Go-Ahead Group Plc, which have risen sharply in recent months.

Labour MP Dale Campbell-Savours said in an early day motion, tabled late Tuesday, that the London Stock Exchange surveillance unit was "seeking to establish why shares in Go-Ahead rose from 361 pence on 15th November to 511 pence on 8 January."
"And in particular, which Go-Ahead directors and other personnel holding information they should not have had, were able to leak price-sensitive information for use in share speculation."

Campbell Savours said in the motion that the LSE had "received information...regarding the working relationship between a group of British Rail managers and senior representatives of the Go-Ahead Group."

"This house believes that this relationship enabled price-sensitive, confidential and privileged information to be made available to the Go-Ahead Group in contravention of rules which should have been followed in the franchising of Regional Railways North East activities."

Go-Ahead group's shares have risen around 40 percent since North Star Transpennine, a consortium of Go Ahead, a North East railways management team and French group Via-GTI, was shortlisted by the British government as a potential bidder for the Regional Railways North East franchise.

Campbell Savours said in the motion that privileged access to information in the accounts of Regional Railways North East was used "to convince those prepared to speculate that Go-Ahead were more likely than other bidders to take over the network."
Go-Ahead Group said Campbell-Savour's motion was "rubbish" and refuted suggestions company directors had "benefited" from any priviledged information.
"Our share price rocketed up with the sector--it had nothing to do with the North East Railways bid," Go-Ahead managing director Martin Ballinger told Reuters.
"It's rubbish, absolute rubbish. I can't think of a more rude word to describe it than that."
The London Stock Exchange has declined to confirm or deny that it was conducting an inquiry into share dealing in Go-Ahead.
